title: The Forbidden Pair
prompt:
**Scenario.** Count binary strings of length n with no two consecutive 1s. Direct construction looks messy. What is the cleanest model?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Enumerate all 2^n strings and filter — n is small anyway

**B)** A DP over positions whose state is 'did the previous position hold a 1?' — the adjacency condition decomposes to one bit

**C)** A number-theoretic formula based on n mod something

**D)** Sort the strings and remove conflicts pairwise

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: The pair-coupled condition decomposes position by position: one bit of state ('prev was 1') captures the entire constraint — classic position DP.
